newsitem.title: UK: N.SEA CRUDES WEAKEN ON IRAQ, BUYER CAUTION.
newsitem.headline: N.SEA CRUDES WEAKEN ON IRAQ, BUYER CAUTION.

text.p: North Sea crudes weakened on Thursday on the prospect of fresh Iraqi exports and buyer caution amid plentiful Atlantic Basin supply, traders said.
A cargo of Brent loading August 20-22 traded sharply down at a 20 cent discount to September Brent, 38 cents under the last reported deal.
The cargo was offered aggressively in the afternoon by a British major at around September -15 cents and was one of only two reported physical deals in thin trade.
"In the North Sea there are almost no buyers," one trader said.
"The weakness is not all to do with Iraq. Even in terms of existing cargoes the supply/demand balance is completely bad (for sellers), and anyway buyers are well covered," said another trader.

A Statfjord loading in the last decade of August changed hands at a confidential price, but traders said it appeared to be close to a 30 cent premium to Dated Brent, little changed from recent valuations.
But most buyers hung back to extract maximum value from an expected further slide in values when Iraq finally manages to load oil from Turkey's Ceyhan and Mina al-Bakr in the Gulf.
Traders expect that to happen next week. Some firms have been lining up tanker charters to start loading Iraqi Kikruk sour from Ceyhan from mid to late August.
"Iraq is pushing people to nominate as early as possible. The first shipments will probably be around August 11-15. They seem willing to accomodate whatever people want," a trader said.

The market's weakness was echoed in the complaint of one trader who said he had offered Brent into the U.S. Gulf on Thursday at the equivalent of a 30 cent discount to September Brent only to be told he would have to come down a further 10 to 20 cents.
